subject: bar chart with means - using ggplot

messages.author: 75db403eb2b8ba68
messages.subject: bar chart with means - using ggplot
parts:
In the help pages hadley provides the following example showing how to
achieve bar charts with y being means of a variable instead of counts.
The example uses qplot however - and not ggplot. Since i would like to
understand ggplot better I would really like to see how this could be
done in ggplot.

# example using qplot
library(ggplot2)
meanprice <- tapply(diamonds$price, diamonds$cut, mean)
cut <- factor(levels(diamonds$cut), levels = levels(diamonds$cut))
qplot(cut, meanprice, geom="bar", stat="identity", fill = I("grey50"))

messages.author: 70ab9fabb9f066d8
messages.subject: Re: bar chart with means - using ggplot
parts:
If you just want to plot the summary data using ggplot then you would do:

ggplot(data.frame(cut, meanprice), aes(cut, meanprice)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "grey50")

If you want to skip the summarising step then one way would be:

ggplot(diamonds, aes(cut, price)) +
stat_summary(fun.y = "mean", fill = "grey50", geom = "bar")

But notice the y-axis extends to the range of price. We can't use
ylim here since it will exclude some of the data which we are
summarising over. So instead use coord_cartesian:

ggplot(diamonds, aes(cut, price)) +
stat_summary(fun.y = "mean", fill = "grey50", geom = "bar") +
coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,5000))

And maybe add in some more breaks in the axis and change its label:

ggplot(diamonds, aes(cut, price)) +
stat_summary(fun.y = "mean", fill = "grey50", geom = "bar") +
coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,5000)) +
scale_y_continuous("mean_price", breaks = 1000 * 0:5)

Charlotte

messages.author: 930dbf41faaa4708
messages.subject: Re: bar chart with means - using ggplot
parts:
I would recommend not representing means by bars at all.

Bars are for counts, stacking from zero. Means are point estimates.
ggplot has a lot of routines for displaying means with errors bars:
geom_linerange, geom_pointrange. To hone your ggplot skills I
recommend looking into these geoms.
